Data frames

Source: R/io-values-dataframe.R
io-dataframe.Rd

Reads and writes the Element dataframe, version 0.2.0, a group with the attributes _index and column-order, one member per column and one for the index. Its R values are S4Vectors::DataFrame (read and written) and data.frame (written).

Usage

write_dataframe(store, key, value, dataset_kwargs, path)

Arguments

store

An open rhdf5 file or group handle.

key

Name of the Element within store, "/" writes into the root.

value

The R value to write.

dataset_kwargs

A list of dataset creation options.

path

Path of the Element within store.

Details

The index is the row names, with the index name in metadata() under index_name (the index_name attribute of a data.frame). The member is called _index when there is no index name. Row names that are NULL (or automatic for a data.frame) are written as Python writes a RangeIndex, an int64 array of 0 to n - 1. An index that is not a plain string vector (integer, categorical or a string-array) is kept in metadata() under index_source and written back as it was, as long as the row names still match it.

Columns follow the rules of the Elements they are written as. A character column is a nullable-string-array as pandas 3 writes a str column, unless it was read from a plain string-array or the setting allow_write_nullable_strings is FALSE (see io-nullable). A column must be a vector without a dim of more than one dimension, and column names must be unique and not _index.
